summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY with gateway-driven self-update in obfuscated agent bundle
details: Package @whalent/agent-core@0.3.264 ships a ~13 MB fully obfuscated CommonJS bundle at dist/index.cjs (declared as both main and bin) that wires a WebSocket client to a remote gateway (URL from WHALENT_GATEWAY / CODEX_AGENT_GATEWAY / CLAUDE_AGENT_GATEWAY, auth via WHALENT_TOKEN) and connects it to node-pty and ssh2. Message handlers include 'register', 'heartbeat', 'daemon', and 'upgrade'. When the CLI runs, whoever controls the configured gateway can drive an interactive PTY and shell on the host executing the agent. A separate 'upgrade' code path reads WHALENT_NPM_REGISTRY / NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY and, per the README statement that the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades', allows the gateway operator to push arbitrary new versions of the package from a caller-configured registry and load them as the running daemon — a remote code-injection channel by design. The entire runtime bundle is heavily obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style rotated string arrays, hex identifiers, and control-flow flattening (~402k transforms across a 16-module webpack bundle), concealing destination hosts, message types, and shell dispatch logic from static inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
